rationale: Evidence from the last race (entityR2A score 124.80, up from 57.10): the widened sensor spread (x = ±0.024 m), the 0.016 m footprint, kd 0.30 and base_speed 1.5 helped. One of 60 runs finished, on the oval. Off-track is still the failure mode on all three tracks, and line losses persist: 1.1 per run on the oval, 2.0 on the s-bend and 1.0 on the slalom. Max error is still about 0.061 to 0.063, just above the 0.06 m limit. Steering oscillation rose to 0.17 on the oval and 0.23 on the s-bend, from 0.11 to 0.16 at baseline. That is a moderate rise, not a jump, so I am not reducing kd yet. The Evaluator's stated next step applies: line losses are still present and max_error is still above 0.06, so raise kp from 3.0 to 3.5 with kd held at 0.30 and the widened spread kept. Stronger proportional steering should pull the robot back before the error reaches the line-loss threshold on bends. Speed stays at 1.5, because the oval finishes in about 1.87 s, so speed is not the binding constraint yet. Expected result: line_loss_events fall, max_error drops below 0.06 on at least some tracks, and completions rise on the oval and possibly the s-bend. Risk: oscillation may rise further. If it does, the next step is kd 0.2 before any change to kp. Hypotheses: H1, the drift on bends is proportional to the error and is cut by higher kp. H2, the remaining line losses happen on the tightest bends, where the signal is weakest. Measurements wanted next: per-track completion and progress, max_error and where it peaks, line-loss timing, and steering oscillation to judge the kp/kd balance.
